Team —

As we lock the QBR deck for next week I want a tight one-pager we can show Execs that explains our infra capacity posture and the unit economics levers. Specifically I want: 

- Current committed GPU spend (monthly run-rate) and utilization by pool (hosted vs dedicated).
- Levers and estimated delta to $/1000 tokens from: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization change, and routing to cheaper variants.

- 90/10 forecast for next quarter (baseline vs optimized).

Marcus: can you produce the cost sheet (month-to-date) + utilization by cluster and attach?
Laura: please call out any enterprise deals (AtlasCloud) that need reserved capacity or SLAs that change unit math.
Hannah: ops, call out any infra constraints (disk, network egress) that would block batching/cache rollout.
Stephanie: any relevant topline messaging for execs (revenue impact vs. savings).

Target: deliver a review-ready one-pager and attached cost workbook by EOD Thu (25 Feb). I will synthesize into the QBR slide. If we can't hit full model, prioritize gross $ change per lever and impact on latency SLOs.

Thanks,

Vivek —

Uploading first-pass numbers. Summary here:

- Current committed GPU spend (Feb MTD): $2.18M monthly run-rate across hosted + dedicated. Hosted = $1.26M (58%), Dedicated = $0.92M (42%).
- Utilization (90-day lookback, weighted by token-time): Hosted pools avg 48% (p95 74%), Dedicated pools avg 61% (p95 83%).

Levers (rough estimates, conservative):
- Batching (improved batching config + dynamic windowing): ~12–18% reduction in $/token at baseline workloads; risk: 10–15ms tail added for small interactive flows.
- Prefix/KV caching (enable hot-prefix caching across sessions): ~8–14% reduction; risk: cache invalidation complexity + memory footprint in the serving runtime.
- Quantization (move select models from int8->4-bit experimental): ~22–30% reduction in model compute; risk: quality regressions on generation (needs eval A/B).
- Routing to cheaper variants (auto-fallback to quantized or smaller model for low-risk routes): ~6–10% delta; risk: customer-visible quality delta.

Attached: infra_cost_model_v2.xlsx (tabs: summary, per-cluster, lever-simulations). The lever sims assume 70% safe adoption rate.

I also added baseline sensitivity: if utilization improves +10p (e.g., from 48% -> 58%) we see ~9% effective $ reduction due to amortization of fixed GPU time.

Marcus
Senior PM, Serving Economics

Quick ops note — from an operational constraints perspective: 

- Batching: we can push batching config changes to hosted pools in a staged rollout; critical: need extra headroom on the autoscaler for 48–72 hours during tuning. Ops recommends a 1.2x burst budget to absorb transient latency blips.
- KV cache: adds ~60–90GB RAM per shard in the largest pools; if we enable cross-session prefix caching we need to reserve memory and potentially rebalance shards — low risk but non-zero migration window.
- Network egress: several enterprise customers (AtlasCloud included) incur egress costs that increase with caching replication; include those as a small offset in the lever sims.

I've attached a short design doc with scenario timelines — see batching_cache_scenarios.pdf. Ops can perform a canary on the eu-west1 region first (smaller spike exposure) and if stable, promote to us-west.

Hannah
Director, Platform Operations
